title: Bloodlines
essence: Still night: the poet walks out of the Nevermore field into a parade of afro-futurist ancestors who put stars in his hands, and he names them one by one until they are a constellation of his kin. The same nine-point constellation comes back as the Southern-pine joists over the basement mattress he grew up on, as the veins of blood-light in his fingerprint, and as the veining in the marble wings of a gate that finally opens. It is a poem about inheritance getting bigger: a small man under a wide sky becomes a print too big for the frame, then a gate that runs off all four edges.
palette_notes: Night blue #0a1230 and the district colour #2560e1 come from the Ascent sheet (2ce9173b blue city under stars, 5dcae595 milky way over spires). Indigo #2a2f7a is the ancestors' robes. Star white-gold #f4e3b0 is the laundry-rooftop star cluster (e9c68c53) and the nebula in 36c9c157. The single accent #ffc94a is MAE, the heir-light, the one star he is given rather than takes (world module: one accent on one node in every costume; none in M3). Ember #e08a3c is the bonfire under the ribbed arch in 36c9c157 (parade lantern glow). Southern pine #b9874f and the basement's dark #3a2a22 are from the cramped wood-and-concrete stairwell 34a1d5c3. Marble #e8e4dc for the winged gate.

full_text.line: They tell me to ask if I can inherit the earth,
to ask if I can name my own stars, even galaxies if I may.
The past too was waiting for me.
Coming of age in the shared rooms of human basements
as bedrooms, mattress pads where the wood beams
of southern pine could comfort my spine, it didn't.
To dream was to prevail.
They tell me to ask if I can invent a new universe,
to ask if God would let me, little old me,
award a blessing here or there.
Even grant miracles where the needs
of the spoken word exists.
In uncertain times, in forsaken times,
in tears that spoke in lieu of forbidden lines,
or a history too battered and bruised to travel.
To dream was to prevail.
Their blood flows through my hands.
Fingerprints that orchestra great powers,
they tell me, sun kissing my skin
and deepening my voice to a baritone of a million cries,
to an unanswered plight.
Beware of me.

insights: One graph, four costumes: lay out the nine-node constellation once (KIN coordinates in the world module) and reuse it as sky, joists, fingerprint veins and marble veining. The eye recognises it before it can say why; that is the poem's continuity.

Scale is the arc: lock the camera and grow the subject (small man, wide sky in M1 -> print larger than frame in M4 -> gate past all four edges in M5). Cut-out makes this cheap: same cards, bigger prints.
Spend the single accent (#ffc94a) only on Mae's star, wherever it is; M3 gets none because he owns nothing yet.
The basement must be uncomfortable without being sad-coloured: keep it in the same blue night with one warm bulb, and let the window well show the named stars so the past is still under his sky.

The gates stanza is spoken at the head of the 06 reading (06 recording 00:00.0), while 05's film and world module stage it as 05's final movement; cut the gate opening to that line so the two poems hand off across it.
Avoid a spray of stars: named stars are holes of light, unnamed ones stay tiny specks; a ring of evenly spaced stars reads as diagram, not family.
Ancestors' hands on his are the most intimate image in the suite so far; give the hand cards real weight and slow timing.
future: The winged marble gate is the entrance to Atlantis in 06 (same leaves, opened).
The star_orb becomes the soul-lights and the comet spark in 06 and the beacon on the capital dome.
The ancestors return as the remembered elders of 12 and the elders at prayer in 13 (same robe cards, softer light).
The constellation layout can be reused as the city's street grid or a plaza mosaic in 06.
The basement and the mattress pad come back for any childhood memory in 09.
